scope: Theorem 4.2 (Boundary compression) of the manuscript “Filtered products and boundary-preserving compression in complex cobordism” (preprints/Filtered-products-and-boundary-preserving-compression-in-complex-cobordism-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 302 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c47745026b3a083c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let P be a finite polyhedron, let f : P → C(t, n) be PL, and fix 0 < a < 1/16. If ωMU f, Zan(t, n)  = 0, then for arbitrarily large positive integers u there is a continuous map G : Pu −→ C(t, un) with the following properties. At every point of Pu, at least (a/8)un output slots are on their cube boundaries. Moreover, if any slot of f×u is on its boundary, the corresponding slot of G equals that original slot exactly.
